title: Tip-to-Self Rebounding
description: Seated players learn to tip a high rebound up and toward their own chair with one hand, then secure it with two, a key technique when opponents' reach is similar and the ball is above everyone.

content.objective: Control a rebound you cannot catch cleanly by tipping it up and toward yourself, then securing it with two hands before an opponent can.
content.setup: Rebounder in front of the rim at the right block; coach shoots from the elbow; later a competing rebounder.
content.organization: Five shots per rebounder, then rotate; progress to two rebounders competing.
instructions: The coach shoots and misses off the rim.
Position the chair under the likely landing spot and reach with the outside hand.
Tip the ball up and back toward your own chair with the fingertips.
Catch the tipped ball with two hands and pull it into the lap.
Pivot the chair away from pressure and outlet.
coachingPoints: Tip up and toward yourself, not out.
Use the fingertips, keep the wrist firm.
Two hands to secure, ball into the lap.
commonMistakes: Slapping the ball away from the rim.
Reaching so far that the chair tips.
Securing with one hand and losing the ball.
content.safety: Anti-tip casters fitted; rebounders keep both wheels down when reaching; no ramming other chairs.
progressions: Competing rebounder on the same spot.
Tip-in to score instead of securing (offensive version).
regressions: Coach tosses the ball high off the backboard.
successCriteria: Chair stays stable on every reach.
content.gameApplication: When several players reach at the same height, the one who tips the ball to themselves wins the rebound.
